headline: Adam Mosseri says negativity around AI is ‘going to get worse’
summary: Instagram head Adam Mosseri acknowledges growing public dislike for AI. He notes negativity isn't limited to youth or creatives. Mosseri discussed this trend on the Colin and Samir podcast.

headline: A hacker stole more than 40,000 DHS employee records
summary: A hacker breached the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). Over 41,000 employee records, including names and contacts, were stolen. Data from ICE and CBP staff was compromised in the breach.

headline: Akai is embracing vibe-coded mods with an open-source MPC
summary: Akai is championing 'vibe-coded' modifications for its new MPC Sample Key. The company is providing early access to modders and custom firmware developers. The upcoming device will feature open-source firmware, encouraging community creativity.

headline: Readwise is taking on Kindle and Kobo for ebook supremacy
summary: Readwise, known for highlight organization, is launching Readwise Books. The new platform aims to compete directly with Kindle and Kobo ebook stores. Readwise also offers Readwise Reader for articles and newsletters.

headline: BioWare Co-Founder Speaks Out on Studio Closure, Mass Effect Cancellation
summary: BioWare co-founder Greg Zeschuk comments on the recent studio closure. 50 jobs were lost, part of 400 company-wide cuts. The unannounced Mass Effect 5, titled 'Mass Effect: Universe', was cancelled.

headline: Original Donkey Kong Poster That Was Nearly Thrown Away Sold at Auction for Record-Breaking $329,400
summary: A rare 1981 Donkey Kong promotional poster sold for $329,400 at auction. It marks the most expensive piece of original video game art ever sold. The poster features Mario's very first public appearance.

headline: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 DMZ Review
summary: A review details the new DMZ mode in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. The mode is described as a significantly improved extraction shooter. It offers a "bigger and better" experience than previous iterations.

headline: Kane Parsons Confirms Meetings With Valve, But Won't Adapt Their Games If It Can't Be Done Right
summary: "Backrooms" director Kane Parsons confirms discussions with Valve. He stated he would only adapt Valve IPs if quality could be ensured. Parsons is cautious about adapting games if it can't be done "right."

headline: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget
summary: Chancellor Healey announced a £100 payment for energy bills. His first Budget also includes a new bank tax. Measures aim to address the cost of living amidst economic turmoil.

headline: I earn £30,000. I'm angry there was no fuel duty cut in the Budget
summary: Citizens express frustration over the absence of a fuel duty cut in the new Budget. Individuals across various income brackets shared their reactions. Many feel the Budget did not adequately address everyday costs like fuel.

headline: High-speed train crash kills at least 68 people in Spain
summary: A high-speed train crash in Spain resulted in at least 68 fatalities. The transport minister attributed the collision to an "inexplicable" error. One train struck another that was stationary on the tracks.

headline: Netanyahu's bloc leading Israel election but short of majority, partial results show
summary: Netanyahu's bloc is leading the Israeli election, per partial results. With 85% of ballots counted, they secure 53 seats in the Knesset. The bloc is currently short of a majority in the 120-seat parliament.
